forces.title: AI shifts ad value from impressions to intelligent selection
forces.description: AI is fundamentally reshaping the advertising economy by moving the focus from merely securing data-driven impressions to being actively 'surfaced, recommended, and selected' by AI systems. This implies that success for advertisers, and consequently the ad tech supporting them, will increasingly depend on optimizing for AI algorithms that shape consumer discovery and purchasing decisions, rather than traditional impression-based metrics.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: AI-driven direct buying bypasses programmatic intermediaries
forces.description: The rise of AI is accelerating a trend towards direct media deals, with advertisers increasingly bypassing programmatic intermediaries and agencies. Integrated platforms (walled gardens) and AI-native platforms offer automated targeting, closed-loop measurement, and transaction visibility, leading to a compression of the ad tech middle. This reduces the role of traditional DSPs, SSPs, and ad exchanges, as 82% of surveyed advertisers plan to buy AI ad formats directly.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: Ad tech middle compresses due to AI-native buying agents
forces.description: AI-native buying agents are capable of replicating cross-platform optimization within a single workflow, which is leading to the elimination of key use cases for traditional ad tech components like SSPs, exchanges, and undifferentiated middleware. This 'compression of the ad tech middle' suggests a significant structural challenge for pure-play ad tech firms that rely on arbitrage and intermediation across platforms, forcing a re-evaluation of their core value proposition.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: Opportunity in neutral cross-platform connective infrastructure for ad tech
forces.description: Amid increasing consolidation into walled gardens and AI platforms, a significant opportunity emerges for ad tech to act as a neutral 'connective tissue'. This involves providing independent, cross-platform identity, measurement, and AI performance audit services. Advertisers will continue to value unbiased tools to compare performance and manage spend across diverse ecosystems, making neutrality and robust governance key competitive differentiators for specialized ad tech providers.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: Ad tech can specialize in AI-native bidding and clean-room partnerships
forces.description: To adapt to the agentic advertising economy, ad tech firms are advised to specialize in a neutral infrastructure layer. This includes developing advanced AI-native bidding solutions that optimize for outcomes rather than just impressions, and fostering clean-room partnerships for secure data collaboration. This strategic pivot allows ad tech to re-anchor its pricing models around usage or verifiable outcomes, differentiating itself from commoditized middleware and offering crucial value to advertisers navigating complex data environments.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: Advertiser spend shifting from open web to integrated platforms
forces.description: Roughly 40% of reallocated AI-driven ad spend is moving away from traditional search and the open web towards integrated platforms (walled gardens) that offer stronger data, measurement, and transaction capabilities. This structural shift diminishes the available inventory and intermediation opportunities for pure-play ad tech on the open web, compelling them to adapt their offerings to either integrate with or provide neutral services across these more powerful, closed ecosystems.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: AI anticipated to boost total media spend and ROAS for advertisers
forces.description: A significant majority of advertisers (75%) expect AI to increase their total media spend, and one-third anticipate at least a 10% increase in Return on Ad Spend (ROAS). This general optimism about AI's ability to drive efficiency and effectiveness in advertising creates a favorable environment, as a larger, more efficient overall ad market can translate into more budget for specialized ad tech solutions that can demonstrate clear value and outcomes.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: Music streaming shift from ad-supported to subscription models
forces.description: The music streaming industry is undergoing a structural shift towards subscription-based monetization, moving away from advertising revenue. Users are increasingly willing to pay for music to avoid ads and access premium features, with ad avoidance being a primary driver for paid subscriptions. This trend reduces the available ad inventory and the overall advertising revenue pool in the music streaming segment, posing a headwind for ad tech providers reliant on this inventory.
forces.source_title: How India can unlock the next phase of music streaming growth

viewpoints.title: AI to reshape ad tech, compressing intermediaries as direct buying rises
viewpoints.description: McKinsey expects AI to significantly transform the ad tech ecosystem, leading to compression of the 'ad tech middle'. AI-native buying agents, capable of cross-platform optimization within a single workflow, are projected to eliminate key use cases for traditional supply-side platforms (SSPs), exchanges, demand-side platforms (DSPs), and undifferentiated middleware. This shift implies advertisers increasingly bypass programmatic intermediaries for direct deals, reinforcing the trend of consolidation within walled gardens and AI-native platforms. Ad tech firms must adapt by specializing in neutral infrastructure layers.
viewpoints.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

viewpoints.title: Ad tech relevance hinges on neutral cross-platform identity and measurement services
viewpoints.description: McKinsey suggests that to remain relevant amid AI-driven advertising shifts and the rise of walled gardens, ad tech companies must focus on providing neutral, cross-platform infrastructure. This includes robust identity solutions, clean-room partnerships, and independent measurement capabilities that allow advertisers to compare performance and manage spending across diverse, closed ecosystems. Trust and governance are emerging as critical competitive differentiators, with opportunities in offering AI performance audits and validation services to ensure transparency.
viewpoints.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

demand_drivers.description: The expanding digital media landscape (OTT, social, gaming) drives a larger overall pool of digital ad spend, creating a base for ad tech services.

market_sizing.methodology: Crisil Intelligence reported India's total advertising industry surpassed Rs. 1,00,000 crore (US$ 11.41 billion) in FY25, with digital media accounting for nearly 46% of total ad spend. This figure represents the overall digital advertising spend, which pure-play ad tech operates within but does not exclusively capture, as much also goes to platforms owning the audience (IN090301).
market_sizing.source_title: Media and Entertainment Industry In India

demand_drivers.description: Small and medium enterprise (SME) marketers are increasing their digital advertising budgets and utilizing online shopping channels more, boosting demand for performance-based digital ad solutions.
A significant 50% increase in e-commerce advertising signals a growing channel for digital ad spend, often requiring sophisticated ad tech to optimize performance and reach.

market_sizing.methodology: Reported digital advertising growth of 17% in 2024, reaching Rs. 70,000 crore (US$ 8.04 billion), with e-commerce advertising experiencing a 50% increase. This indicates the overall market for digital advertising, not exclusively pure-play ad tech, but the growth trend impacts the operational environment for ad tech providers.
market_sizing.source_title: Media and Entertainment Industry In India

demand_drivers.description: India's total advertising market is projected for substantial growth, indicating an expanding pool of budget that ad tech can tap into, especially as digital channels continue to gain share.

market_sizing.methodology: Analysis of trends in the overall advertising market, including projections for digital media. While not a direct market size for pure-play ad tech, it indicates the total advertising expenditure influencing the demand for ad tech services.
